feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital leadership roles: it shows clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector/platform expertise. It is well written overall, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style inconsistencies and limited quantified outcomes beyond activity/scale.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia operations.  
- Strong credibility through concrete platforms and tools: Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Clarity, AI search, and studio/video operations.  
- Good strategic positioning in the header and competencies; the profile quickly communicates niche value in public-sector digital modernization.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities or outputs, but fewer show business/user impact (e.g., engagement lift, efficiency gains, adoption, cost savings, search success improvements).  
- Reduce duplication across “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidating these would improve structure and scannability.  
- Fix stylistic inconsistencies: “Coleman DAVIS” capitalization is unusual; punctuation in bullets is inconsistent; “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” reads awkwardly; “10×20-foot” may be clearer as “10 x 20-foot.” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and sector focus, but it reads slightly generic and overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and recent NACo experience. It would be stronger with one concrete scale signal and tighter phrasing.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “Senior digital leader” with a more specific positioning tied to public-sector/platform leadership.
- Add one proof point from recent experience, e.g., “10,000+ page Drupal migration,” “3.5M annual page views,” or “50+ internal publishers.”
- Tighten the list of responsibilities to avoid sounding like a skills dump; group related areas.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems. Leads enterprise website transformation, digital governance, analytics and editorial operations for mission-driven organizations, including a 10,000+ page Drupal migration supporting 3.5M annual page views and 50+ internal publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” repeats ideas already covered in Core Competencies and Recent Projects.
- The opening closely echoes the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. It will be more effective if tightened, made more distinctive, and aligned to the most senior/recent strengths.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace broad phrases with sharper, leadership-level terms: “Enterprise web modernization,” “Digital governance and editorial operations,” “Analytics, reporting, and decision-support infrastructure.”
- Group overlapping items to reduce sprawl and improve scanability; suggested version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and optimization infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- Standardize style: use “and” instead of mixing “&” with “and”; keep all items as noun phrases.
- Consider dropping “Advocacy” unless targeting advocacy-heavy roles specifically; “public-sector communications” is broader and already well supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization” and “AI-enabled…experiences” closely duplicate the header.
- Several items overlap heavily with Topline Skills and Technical + IT, especially analytics, automation, multimedia, and communications.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads like a compressed repeat of the recent consulting and NACo experience. Tightening the formatting and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinct and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a simple lead-in and consistent structure: project name + action + result/focus area.
- Replace generic phrasing like “built”/“developed” with more differentiated verbs such as “launched,” “architected,” or “produced.”
- Clarify scale or purpose where possible: audience, campaign function, platform, or organizational value.
- Fix style consistency: use “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently; spell out “10 x 20-foot” instead of “10×20-foot” for CV readability.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with recent Work Experience bullets; consider reframing this section as selected examples with sharper outcomes.
- The anniversary campaign is the most distinct item here; keep that level of specificity across all four projects.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the project footer and prior NACo entries. Tighten around strategic ownership, technical depth, and 1–2 concrete outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary line: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on enterprise web strategy, digital operations, and campaign platform development across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 4 impact-focused bullets; e.g. combine systems/workflows/analytics/governance into one line about improving cross-channel coordination and publishing operations.
- Rephrase technical work to show ownership: “Built Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing resource hubs.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, users served, workflow time reduced, publishing speed improved, search relevance gains, or adoption metrics for the AI search initiative.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search initiative” and Drupal microsite work duplicate the Recent Projects section; keep this entry higher-level and let the footer hold named examples.
- Governance/analytics/enterprise web improvement also echo the 2022–2024 NACo role; emphasize new consulting scope or advisory capacity.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation outcomes, and avoid repeating channel-management points covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope/result line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Reorder bullets to lead with the website modernization and analytics buildout; these are the clearest enterprise-level achievements.
- Make outcomes more measurable where possible: add email list size/open-rate gains, social growth/engagement, video output volume, budget size, team size, or reporting efficiency improvements.
- Tighten phrasing for concision, e.g. “Led redesign and Drupal migration of a 10,000+ page site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director entry; either add stronger outcomes here or cut it.
- Video/studio language may partially duplicate the footer project list; keep this version focused on organizational capability built.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. To add value, emphasize what was built or expanded at this level and quantify scope/results where possible.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from broad ownership to advancement: “Scaled NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy reach.”
- Tighten bullets and make them outcome-led:
- Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Launched/grew a weekly advocacy video update into a recurring policy communications channel distributed across [web/email/social].
- Built cross-team editorial planning processes linking communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Standardized digital publishing workflows to improve consistency, speed and coordination.
- Add metrics if available: subscriber growth, open rates, video views, publishing volume, turnaround time, or number of teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Video updates” overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; distinguish this as scaling/formalizing the program.
- “Workflows/governance” overlaps with the Director role; keep this entry focused on implementation and cross-team coordination.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent experience. Tighten it to emphasize senior leadership scope and distinctive strengths not already repeated elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications
- Editorial governance and scalable content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership across web, email, social and video
- Advocacy and member-facing messaging strategy
- Audience-centered content planning and information design
- If space allows, make one line outcome-oriented, e.g. “Digital strategy for 10,000+ page platforms and multi-team publishing environments.”
- Use parallel noun phrases; avoid mixing broad leadership terms with vague descriptors like “audience-focused.”
- Consider swapping “public-sector and advocacy messaging” for “mission-driven communications strategy” if you want broader applicability beyond government associations.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” duplicate Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weakly differentiated from the header’s “content operations” and “user experiences.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and execution themes tied to recent Drupal modernization and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter, impact-oriented list: Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations & workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences
- Put the most relevant/recent strengths first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations, and AI-enabled search; demote older or less central platforms.
- Use parallel phrasing; avoid mixing platforms, coding languages, and outcomes in random order.
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented: AI-enabled search and structured content discovery

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation.”
- “Workflow automation” also overlaps with Core Competencies; keep this version shorter and more strategic.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making value, not just tool names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a tool list to an outcomes-oriented line, e.g.: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio & Microsoft Clarity • KPI framework design • executive/leadership dashboards • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “executive dashboards” or “executive reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- Consider changing “KPI design” to “measurement strategy & KPI design” if space allows; it signals higher-level ownership.
- If you can support it elsewhere, add one impact cue such as “analytics infrastructure for 10,000+ page site” in experience bullets rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies and “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT.
- Avoid repeating the exact same tool stack in both Topline Skills and Technical + IT; use Topline Skills for strategic framing, Technical + IT for full tool inventory.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This skill block is relevant, but it’s generic and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies plus multiple NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing delivery scope and higher-value capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with tighter, more senior phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event production workflows”
- If accurate, add scale/outcome language instead of generic nouns, e.g. “In-house studio production” or “Recurring advocacy video and livestream delivery”
- Consider swapping “Video production and editing” for “Broadcast-quality video production” to better match the Director-level studio build in recent experience
- Keep only 4 items max and group related terms to reduce listiness

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This repeats “Multimedia production and livestream operations” from Core Competencies almost verbatim
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “Livestreaming”; combine them rather than listing separately

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s generic and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Use this space to signal depth and recency, especially Drupal, which is central to recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: Drupal (enterprise migrations, modular content architecture) • WordPress • SharePoint • Microsoft Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- If space allows, prioritize by strength/relevance: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
- Consider adding proficiency cues only where defensible, e.g., “Drupal (10,000+ page migration; microsite builds)” to tie the skill to impact
- Standardize naming: “Microsoft Power Pages” is clearer and more searchable than “Power Pages”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the Topline Skills entry “Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists Drupal, WordPress, and SharePoint
- “CMS modernization” in Topline Skills already conveys platform breadth; avoid repeating the same list in both sections unless this version adds specificity

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. For a senior digital leader, this item should emphasize implementation strengths most relevant to recent work and de-emphasize older/basic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Front-End & Technical Implementation
- Tighten and modernize phrasing: HTML/CSS • JavaScript/jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- If accurate, add scope/outcome language instead of only tools, e.g. “Front-end implementation, tag management, lightweight serverless scripting, and deployment automation”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless needed for ATS; they add little value at this level

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- “GitHub Actions” may fit better under “Automation & Workflow Systems” unless you want this section focused strictly on implementation/deployment

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems expertise. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools
- Group by function for faster scanning: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier | Jira • Asana • Trello • Basecamp | Slack • Microsoft Teams
- If space allows, add a light qualifier to show applied use, e.g. “workflow automation, project coordination, and cross-team collaboration”
- Consider trimming older/lower-value tools if not used recently; keep the strongest, most current platforms first (e.g. Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams)

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; if space is tight, they add less differentiation than automation/project systems.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful tools to include, but this item is currently just a vendor list and undersells your email leadership. It should signal platform depth without repeating the stronger email achievements already covered in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms
- Tighten and standardize: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of outcomes here: enterprise email automation • newsletter operations • audience segmentation
- Consider a fuller line: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • email automation • segmentation • campaign operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding newsletter scale or audience size here; that impact is already better stated in Director/Associate Communications Director experience.
- Don’t repeat “multi-channel communications” language already covered in Core Competencies and work history.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item mostly repeats the “Topline Skills” analytics section and reads as a keyword list rather than a differentiated technical capability area. Tighten it and emphasize methods/tools over generic terms.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI/dashboard design
- Replace “SEO” with “Google Search Console” or “SEO analysis” to keep this item tool/method-specific.
- Replace “Dashboarding” with “KPI/dashboard design” or “Reporting architecture” for stronger, more senior phrasing.
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this category to impact in experience bullets instead of adding more tools here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Nearly duplicates “Topline Skills – Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider keeping detail in one place and shortening the other.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid expanding this list further without new differentiation.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like setup for later NACo roles. Tighten it around foundational impact, team-building, and concrete outputs without repeating responsibilities covered in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and first-team build: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media function…”
- Make contributions more concrete: specify the website refresh scope, volume/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, and any audience, engagement, or efficiency gains.
- Replace soft phrasing like “high-impact” and “strengthening workflows” with outcomes: e.g., “standardized publishing workflows across web, email, social, and video” or “reduced production turnaround.”
- Suggested version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital media team. Supported a major website refresh, standardized cross-channel publishing workflows, and produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates for member communications. Also provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating newsletter/editorial coordination and advocacy video expansion already covered in the 2018–2022 role.
- “Built/led digital team” overlaps with later leadership entries; keep this one focused on helping establish the function.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened and framed as a foundation in innovation/program support plus emerging digital production leadership.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize ownership and firsts: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities.”
- Make the multimedia work more direct and concise: “Produced digital and multimedia content for organizational communications.”
- Highlight the standout achievement with stronger action verbs: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production planning and episode delivery.”
- If possible, add scope or output metrics: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating broad “digital content production” language already covered in later NACo roles unless you specify this was the first podcast/early multimedia work.
- Don’t overstate digital leadership here; later roles already show the progression into team and platform leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is relevant, but it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Make it more tool-specific and concise so it complements, rather than repeats, broader capability sections.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Multimedia Tools
- Replace with: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator
- If you want to keep one workflow item, use: Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Broadcast/livestream studio systems
- Consider moving “Podcast production” and “Livestream studio workflows” out of this tools list if they’re not software/platform names; they read better as capabilities already covered elsewhere.
